https://telex.hu/after/2026/08/09/heaven.text: Menü Kereső Sohasevolt zene, sohasevolt időből After Fotó: Alföldi Dániel István / Telex Bicsérdi-Fülöp Ádám Ahhoz képest, hogy a halál volt az utolsó színpadon elhangzott szó a Heaven Street Seven visszatérő, ilyen-olyan számítások szerint 30 éves jubileumot ünneplő koncertjén, ez a fellépés inkább azt bizonyította, mennyire élő még ma is a zenekar életműve. Jó kis nosztalgiaiparos húzás az egész – lehetne persze így legyinteni az egészre, és azt mondani, hogy a HS7 se bírta ki, hogy a dalaikba is beivódó nagy kortársak, a Blur, a Pulp, a Supergrass vagy az Oasis visszatérését megirigyelve még egy tiszteletkört fussanak a ma már idősebb, azaz fizetőképesebb törzsközönség előtt. Az ilyen fajta tudatosság és számítás azonban teljesen idegen ettől a zenekartól, és valószínűleg tényleg az van, amiről a frontember, Szűcs Krisztián beszélt a koncert előtti interjúnkban : a zenekar szereti annyira ennek az életműnek a jelentős részét, hogy a dalok megérdemlik néha az ilyen nagyobb gesztusokat, mint amilyen a parkos koncert. Fotó: Alföldi Dániel István / Telex Az ilyen életműösszegző, visszatérő koncerteknél mindig nehéz ügy, hogy mennyire kell az egészből valami különlegeset, valami mást csinálni, mint amit a zenekar korábban egy sima koncertjén tenni szokott. Láthattunk erre az utóbbi években különböző példákat, volt olyan zenekar, amely inkább a zenés színház felé vitte a műsorát, sok extrával, és volt olyan reunion is, ahol szinte jobban egymásra érzett a zenekar, mint a klasszikus korszakában. A HS7 koncertje valahol a két véglet között volt. Akadt például meglepő húzás, amikor a koncert közepén a Hűvös játszotta el a Hol van az a krézi srác? -ot, de az meg szinte pofátlanul minimalista húzás volt, hogy a színpadkép vizualitása megállt egy fekete háttér előtti Heaven Street Seven feliratban. Szóval készült extrákkal a zenekar az alkalomra, előjött Lovasi András a közös dalra, A konyhámban ra, a HS7 Ábrahám Zsolt előtti két gitárosa, Balczer Gábor Cziba és Kiss Endre is közreműködött pár számban, de a koncerten érződött, hogy a zenekar azért nem az ilyen típusú, ünnepeltetős, alkalmi pillanatokban mozog a legotthonosabban. Ezért szerintem a koncert legjobb pillanatai akkor érkeztek, amikor a zenekarnak sem kellett nagyon a koreográfiával, a ki- és belépőkkel törődnie, így tényleg csak a dalokra koncentrált mindenki a színpadon. A koncert kb. egyharmadánál érkező Ez a szerelem/Éjszaka/ Gesztenyefák alatt/Nem elég blokknál lehetett a közönségen is először azt a felszabadultságot érezni, hogy oké, ez most többet jelent mindenkinek az udvarias tisztelgésnél. Fotó: Alföldi Dániel István / Telex Egy ilyen, az ünnepelt zenekar több korszakát is felvonultató koncerten aztán azon is lehet merengeni, hogy mitől talált be ennyi, nagyon különböző embernél a HS7, és hogy maradt ennyire időtálló az életmű nagy része. Mert az még valamennyire magyarázat, hogy a zenekar hangzásából pont kilógó, onnan kikacsintó számok futották be a legnagyobb pályát (Dél-Amerika, Krézi srác, Márta), de közben végig ott volt valami nagyon furcsa együttállás a HS7 zenéjében, ami miatt akkor és ma is kicsit olyan, mintha egy furcsa párhuzamos univerzumból, a sohasevolt idő ből érkezett volna a zenekar. Sok minden ismerős lehet persze ebből a világból, Szűcs dalszerzői attitűdjének alapeleme az irónia, de a legjobb dalszövegeiben ezt a fanyarságot a nonszensszel, a kifacsart, szécsipálos romantikával és költőiséggel párosította. A HS7 zenéje is olyan, amelynek persze fel lehetne sorolni az előképeit, nem is voltak ezek különösebben titokban tartva (a parkos beállás alatt például háromféle zenekaros póló volt a tagokon: Oasis, New Order, Tame Impala), de mindig is olcsó megfejtésnek tartottam a zenekarra a britpopos jelzőt. Főleg a magyar nyelvre váltástól, az áttörést meghozó Cukor lemeztől kezdve lett világos, hogy a zenekar tagjaira jóval a britpop hódítása előttről származó angolszász gitárzenék is nagy hatással voltak, és ugyanúgy építettek ezek a dalok a magyar popzenei és underground hagyományokra. Néha tudatalatt, hiszen a HS7 egyik legjobb száma, az Éjszaka bevallottan csak véletlenül idézi Szörényi Levente és Koncz Zsuzsa azonos című számát. Fotó: Alföldi Dániel István / Telex A HS7-nek biztosan nem kedvezett a maga idejében ez a nehezen leszűkíthető, szerteágazó életmű. Az indie-seknek nem biztos, hogy bejött a kuplé, a Dél-Amerika nagy kedvelői meg nem biztos, hogy csípték a Tudom, hogy szeretsz titokban apokaliptikus hangulatát. Szűcs a könyvében ( Utazás a kegyetlenbe ) például úgy fogalmazott, hogy itthon az üvegplafont csak azzal törhette volna át a zenekar, ha felvesznek valamilyen hiteles pózt, karaktert, és azt tolják végig. Jól látszik, hogy ezzel teljesen ellentétes irányba ment végül a zenekar, és ezért sem egyszerű a HS7-ről véleményt alkotni, mert a zenekar mintha kereste is volna azokat a lehetőségeket, amikor kibújhat az ilyen könnyű magyarázatok, véleményalkotások alól. Jellemző, hogy a talán legegységesebbnek, legkompaktabbnak tartott csúcslemezük ( Tudom, hogy szeretsz titokban ) után kijöttek egy teljesen más irányba induló, kísérletező lemezzel, a Jazz -zel (amin szerintem legalább annyi jó dal és ötlet van, mint az előzőn). Szóval nem lehet csak úgy, egy szusszal a HS7-ről beszélni, a Nem elég például szerintem rossz és irritáló szám, és több olyan daluk is van, amikor vagy csak a refrén, vagy csak a verzé, vagy egy ötlet igazán jó, de minden lemezen ott vannak az olyan, a mostani koncerten is remekül elsülő dalok ( Dunabeat, Hullik a zápor, Nem baj ), amikben a zenekar a saját univerzumán belül talált el nagyon valamit. Fotó: Alföldi Dániel István / Telex Ez a sokszínűség a Parkban is kijött, a zenekar kezdeti időszakát idéző, angol nyelvű számok azért érezhetően nem hozták annyira lázba a közönséget, és nálam az a kitérő sem működött, amikor Szűcs előbb Jappánnal duettben adta elő a Rengeteg bor t, aztán Lovasi érkezett a nem túl emlékezetes közös dalra. A koncert utolsó harmada már nyilván a legnépszerűbb dalokról szólt, a főműsort lezáró Menni kell tovább ra pedig Szűcs már gyerekmotorral érkezett a színpadra, de a koncert ráadásának néhány zavart okozó pillanata („Robi, úgy volt, hogy meghajlunk közösen, nem?”) valahogy igazabb, hitelesebb volt a betervezett gegeknél. Csak eljátszották azért a végén a krézi srácot is, és a szám közben Szűcstől random ponton érkező „tequila!” kiáltás már a régi koncertek idétlenségéből is visszacsempészett valamit a Parkba. Nem tudom, hány év múlva veszi elő ez a felállás újra a HS7 dalait, de azt a koncertet már valahonnan ebből, a zenekarhoz jobban illő és felszabadultabb hangulatból indítanám. http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/31/body-.text: One person died and around 15 people are missing or unaccounted for after a major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced evacuations, swept large boulders into the Colorado River and knocked out the sole water pipeline that serves tourists and residents, the National Park Service said on Sunday.The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered late on Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the park service said without providing additional details. Coroner’s officials were at the scene.Weekend flooding in Arizona’s Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, happened on Saturday afternoon.More than 60 people were evacuated from the depths of the canyon. The park service said it had yet to account for 15 people and asked anyone with details about hikers or campers in the canyon to get in touch.The Arizona Department of Public Safety was helping with additional evacuations on Sunday.Because the main water line was out of service, starting on Monday tourists won't be able to stay overnight at lodges and hotels within Grand Canyon National Park. Year-round residents are being asked to conserve water.“These measures are crucial for ensuring the safety and sustainability of water resources,” the park said in a statement.Torrents of water wiped out footbridges over the creek and altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and extending an existing river rapid or creating a new one.The flood was a major blow to an enduring effort to modernise the pipeline that serves 6 million visitors a year and roughly 1,600 residents of Grand Canyon Village.“Heaven help us if the whole thing down there at the bottom has to be reconstructed,” said Jack Schmidt, director of the Centre for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University.“Where are they going to get the money? It's a nightmare for the park service. And thank God nobody was hurt or killed.”Halting overnight stays at the park because of a lack of water is rare, although the pipeline frequently has failed over the years.A $208 million (€179 million) rehabilitation of the pipeline and upgrades to the associated water delivery system started in 2023, with the park service calling it a crucial investment to ensure the park can meet the needs of residents and visitors. The project was expected to be completed next year.Popular tourist spots, including the Bright Angel Campground, the North Kaibab Trail and Phantom Ranch, home to a historic canteen and dormitories, remained closed on Sunday.Between 1-2.5 cm of rain fell within about 20 minutes on a rocky slope where there’s a steep drop in elevation, said National Weather Service meteorologist Darren McCollum in Flagstaff. The deluge was preceded by two smaller systems that drenched the area hours earlier.“So when the main storm moved in, torrential rain fell on everything that was already soaked, and that caused all the problems that we're seeing," McCollum said.The weather service said the flooding happened on the north side of the Grand Canyon, where Bright Angel Creek comes from the North Rim down to the Colorado River, dropping around 1,828 meters.More rain and thunderstorms were possible for the area into Monday.

https://nypost.com/2026/09/12/entertainm.text: movie review FJORD Running time: 146 minutes. Not yet rated. In theaters Oct. 9. Truth be told, I was a little bjored at “Fjord.” Movies about Scandinavia can have that anesthetizing effect, with their monotonous, stone-faced conversations and cultural aversion to openly expressed emotion. Those herring lovers enjoy nothing more than blankly staring out at the, well, fjord. But Romanian director Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or-winning movie with Oscar buzz now at the Toronto International Film Festival has an enticingly controversial set-up: a local Norwegian government takes away a Christian family’s five kids after teachers spot two bruises on a young girl’s arm. Reasonable, right? Not so fast. There are other possible causes of the injuries. She’s wrestling in gym class, for instance, and the neighbors’ daughter has been pushing teen Elia (Vanessa Ceban) and her brother Emmanuel (Jonathan Ciprian Breazu) to jump out of their bedroom window for kicks. Yet the authorities in the proudly progressive town don’t bother to pursue those other theories, so distrusting of the non-traditional parents they are. More From Johnny Oleksinski Audiences are shrieking bloody murder at ‘Othello’ and howling at ‘Something Rotten!’ at the Stratford Festival ‘Bucking Fastard’ review: Kate and Rooney Mara play freaky sisters in a creepy, self-indulgent mess The cutthroat Oscars battle has begun: Julianne Moore, John Malkovich, ‘The Odyssey’ Even the kids are antagonized by intolerant adults. When Elia casually plucks out “Amazing Grace” on the piano in a classroom, her frigid teacher has the gall to say, “We don’t do evangelizing in school.” Sheesh. And locals are appalled that the Gheorghiu children aren’t allowed to listen to modern music or watch YouTube, as if that alone is tantamount to abuse. Isn’t what they do at home their parents’ decision? An American’s view on these debates will likely differ from a European’s. From my perspective, though, Mungiu’s mostly balanced film, set in an extremely depressing enclave by the sea in Norway, largely sides with the Christians, played by Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve. Shocking! Movies tend to wag their fingers at religious types, not sympathize with or attempt to understand them. 3 A Christian family’s children are taken away from the parents in “Fjord.” Courtesy of TIFF But this also isn’t a “Doubt” or an “Anatomy of a Fall” where we’re never quite sure if the accused actually did the deed. There’s no mystery here to hold our attention, only discourse. Strict dad Mihai (Stan) readily admits he’s slapped his kids on the rear sometimes, and mom Lisbet (Reinsve) swatted her eldest girl’s arm away when she nearly scalded the baby on accident with hot liquid. They insist this is merely a cultural divide, or at worst a spontaneous reaction. Should all five of their kids be taken away and put into foster care over that? Mungiu respects his audience enough to let them decide for themselves who’s in the right as they watch the situation unravel. And they could very well leave without a definite answer. I only wish it unraveled quicker, more compellingly and less repetitiously. Academically I was stimulated by the film’s arguments, but it didn’t get under my skin. The neurons were firing, but the blood wasn’t flowing. 3 Sebastian Stan plays Romanian dad Mihai. Courtesy of TIFF “Fjord,” which Mungiu also wrote, plateaus midway through, long before a trial in the most stunning courtroom of all time is meant to liven things up. It doesn’t really, despite the prosecutor’s string of nasty insults. The couple’s lawyer is their neighbor Mia (Lisa Carlehed), the only person around who will listen to them. Carlehed’s performance is one of the few gentle ones in a story of jagged people, though a subplot with her father-in-law Ake (Øyvind Venstad Kjeksrud) is extraneous padding. He’s there seemingly to restate how much this place sucks. Believe me, we already know. 3 Stan and Reinsve are both terrific. Courtesy of TIFF Reinsve is superb as usual. She was Oscar-nominated, of course, for last year’s Norway-set “ Sentimental Value .” However, Lisbet is far removed from that urbane eccentric — she’s meek, upright and rather joyless. What Reinsve brings to her is sensitivity and palpable love. As for Stan, every time a new role of his is announced you wonder if he lost a bet. In a few short years he’s played a man with a genetic disorder that causes tumors to grow all over his face, a young Donald Trump, Tommy Lee and Bucky Barnes. The parts are all so different, and each time he fully conceals himself beneath them. Stern, soft-spoken and bald Mihai is another impressive transformation. The actor is completely convincing as a Romanian father fighting to tamp down his seething anger as he battles the cold-hearted citizens of freezing Norway. He’s a winter soldier! https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: A home damaged by Hurricane Isaias in Milton, Florida, on 10 October 2026. Photograph: Dan Anderson/EPA View image in fullscreen A home damaged by Hurricane Isaias in Milton, Florida, on 10 October 2026. Photograph: Dan Anderson/EPA Hurricane Isaias Two dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle Deaths came from falling trees as nearly a million people are without power and rain and flooding remain a concern Alba Asenjo Domínguez and agencies Sat 10 Oct 2026 10.34 EDT First published on Sat 10 Oct 2026 10.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Two people have died amid Isaias after it made landfall late on Friday on Florida’s panhandle as a category 2 hurricane, according to authorities. Both of those deaths occurred after trees fell on homes, one in Escambia county, Florida, and another in Birmingham, Alabama, as the storm moved in inland, local officials said. Meanwhile, though it had weakened on Saturday to a post-tropical cyclone, Isaias still posed flooding and tornado threats as it moved inland, forecasters and officials warned. More than 868,000 customers furthermore were without power across Florida, Alabama and Georgia on early Saturday as those in the path of the storm began the cleanup process, according to PowerOutage.us . Although storm surge and tropical storm warnings associated with Isaias had been discontinued, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned there would still likely be “considerable impacts” associated with Isaias across much of southern Alabama, Florida’s panhandle and south-western Georgia . “Flash, urban and river flooding is possible across the region,” the NHC said in a Saturday-morning advisory, adding that there was a considerable potential for flash flooding and landslides across the southern Appalachians. “A risk for tornadoes will persist … through [Saturday] afternoon across parts of the eastern Florida panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas.” Isaias through Sunday is expected to produce rainfall amounts of 4-8in across southern Alabama , Florida’s panhandle and Big Bend regions, and south-west Georgia. Localized totals up to 15in are possible, particularly within rain bands across the Florida panhandle and Big Bend. Across much of the remainder of the south-east US, rainfall amounts of 2-5in are expected, and localized higher amounts up to 10in are possible, especially across the southern Appalachians and coastal Carolinas. Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, on Friday as a potent category 2 hurricane. It was an atypically late-forming first Atlantic hurricane of the season and lashed the US Gulf coast with heavy rain, fierce winds and life-threatening flooding. The hurricane’s maximum sustained winds were 105mph (169km/h), and it was predicted to dissipate on Sunday. Isaias’s winds were so intense they sounded like “a train whistle”, Tim Mowry told the Associated Press after enduring the storm as his home in Pensacola, Florida. Mowry described losing power on Friday afternoon but said could rely on a generator. He said his son tried to drive to his home after his place about 15 minutes away lost power but had to turn around because downed trees and power lines blocked the road. All things considered, Mowry said he was “really fortunate” with respect to how he fared during Isaias. Crestview, Florida, resident Ashley Weeks told the news station WEAR that a tree from her backyard fell on top of her house, damaging the the roof near her daughter’s bedroom and turning the ceiling into piles of debris. It was “just scary – everything, my whole life is in the house”, Weeks said. “We heard a loud … like a bomb went off in the house. It was so loud. And I got up and [saw] the tree through the roof, and it was – freaking out.” Alabama’s governor, Kay Ivey, warned of “possible spinoff tornadoes” and asked residents to “prepare for the worst”. “Right now, we are worried about strong winds, heavy rain and possible spinoff tornadoes in certain parts of the state,” Ivey said. “As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop. We often hear in emergency management: Hope for the best. Prepare for the worst. “That is the approach we need with this particular storm system.” Florida’s governor, Ron DeSantis, said on Saturday that Florida power crews would spend the day assessing damage, clearing roads and performing restoration work. And while the stronger El Niño seemed to limit the number of hurricanes in the Atlantic for the year so far, Isaias forming in October with maximum sustained winds of 105mph marked a stark contrast from historical trends. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) predicted a quiet year in terms of hurricanes at the beginning of a season that officially begins annually on 1 June. Noaa anticipated between three and six hurricanes, well below the average of seven. An August forecast from Noaa cut the expected number to between two and six. Isais is one of the two latest-forming Atlantic hurricanes on record, tying a record set on 8 October 1905. Otherwise, the second-latest date for the first Atlantic hurricane was 11 September – in 2002 and 2013. None of the eight previous named storms of the 2026 Atlantic season intensified above tropical storm status. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas. … More Guided aerial bombs struck residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people , including three children, and injuring at least 18 others, according to Ukrainian officials. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Emergency crews searched damaged apartments, cleared rubble and helped survivors escape as smoke rose over the southern city. Cars were left mangled in the streets and homes were badly damaged, while ambulances ferried the wounded to hospital. The bombardment came amid escalating Russian strikes across Ukraine, which have killed more than 60 people in four days . Missiles also hit Kyiv on Saturday, injuring four people , according to the capital's mayor. The attacks followed US President Donald Trump 's announcement of a deal to buy Russian diesel , which Kyiv warned could help finance Moscow's war . President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of exploiting any easing of economic pressure to continue its attacks.
